knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x y - x + 2 y=-3$. The **normal** line at $\left(-1,-4\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. The product rule gives $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=y+x\frac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y - 1+\left(x + 2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(x + 2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(y - 1\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{y - 1}{x + 2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-5}{1}=5
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{5}=- \frac{1}{5}
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-4\right)&=- \frac{1}{5}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right) \\
y&=- \frac{1}{5}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)+\left(-4\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=- \frac{1}{5}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)+\left(-4\right) \\
x-\left(-1\right)&=-\frac{-4}{- \frac{1}{5}} \\
x&=-21
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(-21,0\right)$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x^{2} - 2 y^{2}=-2$. The **normal** line at $\left(4,3\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 x+\left(- 4 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(- 4 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(2 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{2 x}{- 4 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{8}{-12}=\frac{2}{3}
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{\frac{2}{3}}=- \frac{3}{2}
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(3\right)&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\
y&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(3\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(0-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(3\right) \\
y&=9
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,9\right)$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $2 x^{2} + 2 y^{2}=50$. The **normal** line at $\left(4,-3\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
4 x+\left(4 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(4 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(4 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{4 x}{4 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{16}{-12}=\frac{4}{3}
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{\frac{4}{3}}=- \frac{3}{4}
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-3\right)&=- \frac{3}{4}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\
y&=- \frac{3}{4}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(-3\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=- \frac{3}{4}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(-3\right) \\
x-\left(4\right)&=-\frac{-3}{- \frac{3}{4}} \\
x&=0
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,0\right)$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x y + y^{2}=4$. The **normal** line at $\left(3,1\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. The product rule gives $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=y+x\frac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y+\left(x + 2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(x + 2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(y\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{y}{x + 2 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{1}{5}=- \frac{1}{5}
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{- \frac{1}{5}}=5
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=5\left(x-\left(3\right)\right) \\
y&=5\left(x-\left(3\right)\right)+\left(1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=5\left(0-\left(3\right)\right)+\left(1\right) \\
y&=-14
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,-14\right)$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $3 x^{2} - 2 x + 2 y=37$. The **normal** line at $\left(-3,2\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
6 x - 2+\left(2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(6 x - 2\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{6 x - 2}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-20}{2}=10
$$

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal:

$$
m=-\frac{1}{m_{\mathrm{t}}}=-\frac{1}{10}=- \frac{1}{10}
$$

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(2\right)&=- \frac{1}{10}\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right) \\
y&=- \frac{1}{10}\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right)+\left(2\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=- \frac{1}{10}\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right)+\left(2\right) \\
x-\left(-3\right)&=-\frac{2}{- \frac{1}{10}} \\
x&=17
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(17,0\right)$.
